title: GM diesels in cold weather: fuel pump whine, hard start or stall, P0087 / P2635, gelled fuel (don't replace the pump)
summary: GM bulletin 18-NA-103: winter-incompatible diesel blends gel or form solids that block the in-tank pump pickup, causing pump whine, hard starts, stalls and fuel pressure codes. Warm the vehicle above 32 °F (0 °C); if it starts and the whine is gone, it's the fuel, not the pump.

specs.name: DTCs (K20 ECM)
specs.value: P0087 fuel rail low pressure; P018B fuel pressure sensor performance; P228A / P228B fuel pressure regulator 1/2 control forced engine shutdown; P2635 fuel pump flow performance

specs.name: Thaw target
specs.value: Fuel above 0 °C (32 °F); can take as little as 1-2 hours indoors

specs.name: Covers
specs.value: 2015-2025 GM passenger cars and trucks with diesel engines (not Chevrolet Low Cab Forward medium duty); 2017-2025 Silverado / Sierra 2500/3500

specs.name: Winter additives
specs.value: Must not contain metal-based additives, alcohol or other water emulsifiers

steps.text: Bring the vehicle inside and let the fuel warm above 32 °F (watch fuel temperature on the scan tool). Once it starts, warm return fuel helps thaw the tank.
Confirm it starts and the pump whine is gone, then drain the water separator at the bottom of the fuel filter.
Don't replace the in-tank fuel pump for this. If warming the fuel cured it, the fuel blend didn't suit the weather; buying from high-volume stations helps keep fuel fresh.

body: GM treats this as a local fuel issue, not a vehicle defect, and says not to submit a warranty claim for it. In Canada, #1 diesel is Type A (winter) and #2 is Type B (summer).

sources.title: Service Bulletin 18-NA-103: Information on Diesel Fuel Gelling in Cold Temperatures Causing In-Tank Fuel Pump Whine and Driveability Concerns
sources.citation: Condition, cause, correction and service recommendation pp. 1-2; NHTSA ID 11006604
